facts.statement: Iberodactylus is classified as a pterodactyloid pterosaur within the clade Anhangueria.
facts.quote: Iberodactylus is a genus of pterodactyloid pterosaurs belonging to the clade Anhangueria

facts.statement: Iberodactylus lived during the Early Cretaceous in the region of modern-day Spain.
facts.quote: during the Early Cretaceous lived in the area of present Spain

facts.statement: Amateur paleontologist Javier Andreu discovered the skull of Iberodactylus at the Los Quiñones site near Obón in Aragón in the late 1980s.
facts.quote: In the late 1980s, amateur paleontologist Javier Andreu discovered a pterosaur skull at the Los Quiñones site, 1 km west of Obón in Aragón

facts.statement: The species Iberodactylus andreui was formally named and described in 2019 by a team including Borja Holgado and Alexander Wilhelm Armin Kellner.
facts.quote: In 2019, the type species, Iberodactylus andreui, was named and described by Borja Holgado, Rubi Vargas Pêgas, José Ignacio Canudo, Josep Fortuny, Taissa Rodrigues, Julio Company and Alexander Wilhelm Armin Kellner

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in the Barremian-aged chalkstone layers of the Blesa Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype, MPZ-2014/1, was found in a chalkstone layer of the Blesa Formation dating from the Barremian

facts.statement: The genus name combines a reference to Iberia with the Greek word for 'finger'.
facts.quote: The generic name combines a reference to Iberia with a Greek δάκτυλος, daktylos, meaning "finger"

facts.statement: The specific name honors the discoverer, Javier Andreu.
facts.quote: The specific name honors Andreu as discoverer

facts.statement: When discovered, the fossil represented the most complete pterosaur find in Spain aside from Prejanopterus.
facts.quote: At the time it represented the most complete discovery of pterosaur fossil material in Spain apart from the remains of Prejanopterus

facts.statement: Iberodactylus was the largest pterosaur known from the Iberian Peninsula until 2019.
facts.quote: This would make Iberodactylus the largest pterosaur found in the Iberian Peninsula up to 2019

facts.statement: Iberodactylus had an estimated wingspan between 375 and 404 centimeters.
facts.quote: The extrapolations indicated a wingspan that measured between 375 and 404 cm

facts.statement: The wings of Iberodactylus were estimated to be about 4 meters wide.
facts.quote: From this it was concluded that the paired wings were about 4 m wide

facts.statement: The preserved skull fragment measures 198 millimeters in length and 128 millimeters in height.
facts.quote: The fossil skull fragment has a preserved length of 198 mm and a height of 128 mm

facts.statement: The fossil preserves the base of a crest located on the snout.
facts.quote: The snout bears a crest of which the base alone has been preserved

facts.statement: The bone wall of the crest is approximately 1.5 millimeters thick.
facts.quote: The fracture in the fossil reveals that the bone wall is about 1.5 mm thick

facts.statement: The crest has a triangular cross-section.
facts.quote: The crest is triangular in cross-section

facts.statement: Researchers assumed the specimen was male because the robust crest is considered a plausible display structure.
facts.quote: Because the crest, a plausible display structure, is relatively robust, the authors assumed that the specimen represents a male individual

facts.statement: Holes found on the crest were suggested to be tunnels made by bone-eating beetle larvae.
facts.quote: It was suggested that they could be tunnels made by bone-eating larvae of beetles

facts.statement: The upper jaw bears at least eight conical teeth.
facts.quote: The maxilla bears at least eight conical teeth

facts.statement: Iberodactylus is placed in the clade Hamipteridae within the Anhangueria.
facts.quote: Iberodactylus was, within the Anhangueria, placed in the clade Hamipteridae, named in the same 2019 article

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis recovered Iberodactylus as the sister species of Hamipterus.
facts.quote: It was recovered as the sister species of Hamipterus

facts.statement: Iberodactylus lived between 125.77 and 121.4 million years ago during the Barremian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: Iberodactylus belongs to the suborder Pterodactyloidea.
facts.quote: subordo: Pterodactyloidea

facts.statement: Iberodactylus is part of the unranked group Pteranodontoidea.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Pteranodontoidea

facts.statement: The front edge of the crest on the premaxilla is positioned at an angle of about 80 degrees.
facts.quote: La cresta del premaxilar tiene un borde frontal situado en un ángulo de cerca de 80°

rejected.statement: In 2014, some researchers assumed the holes represented exit holes of a salt gland unique to pterosaurs.
rejected.quote: In 2014, it was assumed that they represented exit holes of a salt gland, unique for the entire Pterosauria
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'represented exit holes of a salt gland unique'

rejected.statement: The teeth increase in size until the third tooth, which is 2 centimeters wide and twice as wide as the first tooth.
rejected.quote: The teeth increase in size until the third tooth, which with a width of 2 cm is twice as wide as the first tooth
